confidence_note: This model (gradient boosting, chosen because it scored best of the two candidates tried) had backtested accuracy (50.3%) that was actually LOWER than simply always predicting the majority class (52.6%) on real held-out test data -- this model showed no real edge and underperformed even the trivial baseline. Treat any direction call from it with strong skepticism, not just mild caution -- it is not a case of 'close but unproven', it actively did worse.
price_confidence_note: This price forecast (linear regression, chosen because it scored best on real held-out test data) had error that was NOT statistically better than simply assuming tomorrow's price equals today's price (Wilcoxon signed-rank test on squared errors). Present the dollar figure as the model's best guess only -- do not imply it is a reliable forecast beyond the current price itself.

implied_volatility_expected_range.methodology_note: Derived from a REAL, professional volatility index (CBOE's Gold/Oil ETF Volatility Index, computed from actual options market prices, same methodology as VIX) using standard square-root-of-time scaling. This is a ONE-STANDARD-DEVIATION range (roughly a 68% likelihood the actual price stays within it, under normal assumptions) -- NOT a guarantee, and NOT a directional signal. It says how far price might move, not which way.

implied_volatility_note: implied_volatility_expected_range is a REAL, market-derived expected price RANGE (from CBOE's Crude Oil ETF Volatility Index, computed from actual USO options prices, same methodology as VIX) -- this describes how FAR price might move over the next period, NOT which direction. It's genuinely different information from the direction/price predictions above (this system's own model outputs) -- never conflate the two.

calibrated_range.note: A calibrated 70% price range for the next trading day: historically the next price landed inside a range built this way about 70% of the time. It says how far price may move, NOT which direction. Live hit rate is tracked in range_live_coverage.

range_live_note: 12/12 live ranges contained the next price so far -- too few to judge calibration yet.
rolling_accuracy_note: Over the last 100 resolved live predictions, this system was correct on direction 42 times (42.0%). This is NOT statistically distinguishable from a coin flip (binomial test) -- treat recent direction calls as having no demonstrated live edge yet.
cross_asset_consistency_note: Oil's direction call (up) and the Dollar Index's direction call (down) point opposite ways, consistent with their typical inverse relationship -- a mild plausibility check passed, not independent confirmation either model is actually correct.
directional_signal_summary: Oil: NO PROVEN EDGE. Treat the direction as a coin flip, not a forecast. Raw model lean: up (84% model score -- an uncalibrated model output, NOT a real probability). Live record: 42% over 100 calls. Calibrated 70% range for the next trading day: 96.04 to 106.81.
directional_edge_research_note: A walk-forward study over 2000-2026 daily data (price + real yield, dollar, VIX, Fed funds, yield slope; 1/5/10/20-day horizons) found no statistically credible, stable directional edge (best ~54-56%, p>0.1).
